overview.description: Fifty-Six (56), known locally as 'Ambathiyaaru', is a complex and highly strategic trick-taking card game popular in the Kerala region of India. An expansion of the simpler game '28', it is played with a double deck of cards and a specialized point-count system from the Jass family. The game is known for its intense bidding phase and the use of 'tables' (physical cards from the unused portion of the deck) to keep track of match scores. It is a partnership game that demands precise card counting and team-wide tactical coordination.

history.origins: Fifty-Six is a South Asian adaptation of the Dutch Jass family of games. It likely reached the Kerala coast through historical trade connections. It evolved from the 28-card variant to include more cards and a higher total point count (56) to accommodate larger groups of players.
timeline: 1700s: Jass games spread globally from the Netherlands.
1900s: 28 becomes a staple of South Asian card culture.
Late 20th Century: Fifty-Six emerges as the 'professional' version of 28 in Kerala social circles.
Present: A centerpiece of communal gaming in Malayali culture.
history.evolution: The game's name comes from the total numerical value of the point cards in the deck (3 points per Jack, 2 per Nine, etc.), which sums exactly to 56.
history.cultural: In Kerala, Fifty-Six is often played in local clubs and during festive gatherings, characterized by loud, aggressive bidding and playful table-talk between partners.

setup.players: 4, 6, or 8 players in two fixed teams. Partners sit alternately.
setup.deck: Two standard decks stripped of all cards below 9. Total 48 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 of each suit, twice). For 8 players, Sevens and Eights are added (Total 64).
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt in three rounds: 8 cards per player initially. Bidding occurs during the dealing process.

rules.objective: Win tricks to capture card points. The bidding team must reach their declared point total to win the round.
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: The player to the dealer's right leads the first card.
2. Must Follow Suit: Players must follow the suit led. If they cannot, they may play any card.
3. Trumps: Trumps are only active once the hidden trump card is revealed. A player who cannot follow suit may ask to 'Reveal Trumps'.
keyRules: No Trump revealed: Until revealed, cards of the 'secret' trump suit have no special power.
Thani: A bid where a player promises to win every single trick alone.
Tables: Match scoring is tracked by transferring low-value cards (2, 3, 4...) between teams.

strategy.basic: Count the Jacks! Since there are 8 Jacks in the double deck (48 or 64 variants), knowing how many have fallen is critical for controlling the endgame.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Hidden Trump' Bluff: Use your weak suits early to force the bidder to reveal trumps. If they reveal a suit they aren't strong in, you can take control of the board.
strategy.advanced: Card Distillation: In a double deck, 'dups' (duplicate cards) are common. Professional players track not just the suit, but which specific duplicate has been played to predict the remaining hand structures.
tips: In 56, the 10 and Ace are equal in points (1). Don't waste a 9 or Jack to save a 10 unless you need to keep the lead.
Partnership communication is key: watch your partner's discards to understand which suit they can reliably win.

list.name: Forced bid
list.description: If you are the last player of the non-dealer's team to bid and everyone before you has passed, you must bid at least 28. By the time the bidding reaches the dealer, there has always been at least one bid.

list.name: Throw in with no points
list.description: If any player has no points (hand consists entirely of Kings and Queens), the cards are thrown in and redealt by the same dealer.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule variant only; no engine constant overrides needed.

list.name: Throw in with all Jacks
list.description: If one player is dealt all eight Jacks, the cards must be thrown in and redealt by the same dealer.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule variant only; no engine constant overrides needed.

list.name: Alternative scoring (40–56)
list.description: Bids from 40 to 55 win 2 or lose 3 tables; a bid of 56 wins 3 or loses 4.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule variant only; no engine constant overrides needed.

list.name: Alternative scoring (40–48)
list.description: Bids from 40 to 48 win 2 or lose 3 tables; all bids of 49 or more win 3 or lose 4.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule variant only; no engine constant overrides needed.

list.name: Redouble times three
list.description: When a bid is redoubled, the basic table score is multiplied by 3 rather than 4.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule variant only; no engine constant overrides needed.

list.name: Cot
list.description: If the winning team wins all the tricks they win twice the usual number of tables. Opponents can offer to surrender before the end of play; if accepted, the winning side gets the ordinary number of tables. If they play on and win all tricks they get double; if they lose any trick they lose double the usual number.

difficulty.easy: Fails to account for the double deck; often confuses the 'secret trump' reveal timing.
difficulty.medium: Tracks Jacks and Nines; bids conservatively around 30; knows when to ask for a trump reveal.
difficulty.hard: Expertly calculates the likelihood of 'Thani' (Grand Slam); uses duplicate cards to bluff suit exhaustion; masters the complex 'Table' scoring system.

considerations: AI must maintain a 'hidden' state for the trump suit until revealed by a legal move.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. You must follow suit if possible; if void in the suit led, you may play any card. The trick is won by the highest trump if any were played, otherwise by the highest card of the suit led. The winner of each trick leads to the next.
play_card.constraints: Only when it is your turn to play to the current trick. Must follow suit when you hold a card of the suit led.

pass.description: Decline to bid; pass the turn to the next player. If everyone passes initially, the hand is played in no trumps and scored as though the dealer's opponents had bid 28.
pass.constraints: Only during the bidding phase when it is your turn.

bid.description: Declare a number of points (28–56) and a trump suit or no trumps. The bidding team must take at least that many card points in tricks to win the round. Each bid must be numerically higher than the previous bid.
bid.constraints: Only on your turn during the bidding phase. Minimum bid 28, maximum 56. Must name a suit or no trumps.

go_out.reason: Game has no going out mechanic.

customActions.description: Deal all cards in batches of four. Each player receives 12 cards in a 4-player game, 8 cards in a 6- or 8-player game.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; after shuffle and cut by the player to dealer's left.

customActions.description: Double the opponent's last bid; table payments are doubled if this becomes the final contract.
customActions.constraints: Only when the most recent bid was made by an opponent.

customActions.description: Redouble after an opponent's double; table payments are quadrupled. Ends the auction.
customActions.constraints: Only when the most recent bid was a double by an opponent of your team's bid.

engine.handRankingSystem: Point-trick: tricks won by highest trump or highest card of led suit; points from J (3), 9 (2), A (1), 10 (1) per trick.
engine.rankingSystem: J-9-A-10-K-Q per suit; 56 total points per deal.
engine.deckDescription: Two 24-card packs (double deck): Aces, Kings, Queens, Jacks, Tens and Nines from two standard 52-card packs (48 cards total for 4 or 6 players). For 8 players, Eights and Sevens are added (64 cards). Cards rank in each suit J-9-A-10-K-Q (high to low).
engine.suitDescription: French suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades. Each suit has six cards (9, 10, J, Q, K, A) per pack in the 48-card variant.
engine.rankDescription: Jass ranking in each suit: Jack highest, then 9, A, 10, K, Q. Point values: Jack 3, Nine 2, Ace 1, Ten 1; Kings, Queens and (in 64-card) 8s and 7s count zero. Total 56 points per deal.
